 Ahead of the Holidays: What to Know
 Published 11:33 am Thursday, November 19, 2026
 By Caroline Weiss 
 ClintonNationalAirportLogo.jpg (Submitted File Photo) 
 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... 
 Travelers across the country are gearing up for arguably one of the busiest traveling times of the year ahead of the fast-approaching holiday season, but there are some things officials would like the public to bear in mind this year.
 According to the Transportation Security Administration (TSA), a slight increase in departing passengers at Clinton National Airport during the Thanksgiving holiday travel period is anticipated, despite uncertain political temperatures and fluctuating fuel prices that have left costs somewhat higher than last year.
 An estimated 47,571 passengers are projected to be screened at the Little Rock airport between Friday, Nov. 20 and Tuesday, Dec. 1. Sunday, Nov. 29 is expected to be the airport’s busiest travel day, with more than 5,200 departing passengers. Monday, Nov. 30 is also projected to be busy, with nearly 4,800 passengers expected to pass through the TSA security checkpoint.
 Thanksgiving travel marks the beginning of the holiday travel season, and passengers are encouraged to plan ahead for a smooth, stress-free experience. Airlines recommend arriving at least two hours before scheduled departure, especially during peak times such as early mornings, or when checking a bag.
 Additional reminders for holiday travelers include:
 Double-check your identification. Arkansas Mobile ID is accepted for identity verification at the TSA checkpoint. Travelers without a REAL ID-compliant form of identification should complete TSA’s ConfirmID process online before heading to the airport.
 Remember the liquid limit. Liquids, gels or aerosols in carry-on bags must be in containers of 3.4 ounces or less and fit inside a single quart-size bag.
 Empty your water bottle. Bring a reusable water bottle but make sure it’s empty before going through security. It can be refilled after screening.
 Watch out for prohibited items. Empty luggage before packing to ensure firearms and other prohibited items are not accidentally left inside. Travelers with questions about permitted and prohibited items can visit tsa.gov for a full list and additional travel guidance.
 Know before you go. Download the airline’s mobile app to stay up to date on flight information and visit the airport’s website for available parking options.
 Guests assisting departing passengers or meeting arriving ones can park free of charge for the first 45 minutes in the East Hourly Lot, conveniently located directly in front of the ticket lobby.
 Similarly, according to the Centers for Disease Control (CDC), overall acute respiratory illness activity across the U.S. is currently low but steadily increasing ahead of Thanksgiving travel, with seasonal influenza (flu) driving the sharpest rise, especially in the state of Louisiana, the only state that had been reported as “Very High.”
 The CDC urges caution ahead of widespread travel, urging public transportation and airline passengers to exercise caution and safety as to not spread airborne illnesses.
 It reports that respiratory illnesses are on the rise across the country ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, with influenza activity increasing earlier than usual this season. National flu test positivity has reached approximately 11.3 percent, while COVID-19 activity remains relatively low at 3.2 percent, despite elevated wastewater levels in some states. RSV activity also remains low nationally, although cases are beginning to increase in some regions.
 In Arkansas and neighboring states, flu activity is moderate and rising, with gradual increases in RSV cases. Health officials encourage residents to stay current on recommended vaccinations, practice good hygiene and avoid close contact with others when sick. Older adults, young children and people with underlying health conditions face the greatest risk of serious complications.
